clue.text: Rubbish stuffed, say, by recess when heading off

parts.note: to have stuffed oneself is to have gobbled food down
say is the usual signal for e.g., for example

indicators.note: a thing heading off loses its front, so the word for recess drops its first letter

parts.note: a nook is a small recess or alcove

explanation.surface: Someone complains that the stuff crammed into an alcove is nothing but junk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when heading off' trims the N from NOOK, leaving OOK.
explanation.definitionFit: Gobbledegook is meaningless jargon or nonsense, so rubbish in the sense of empty talk.

clue.text: Doctor in the morning enters old institute folding paper

indicators.note: the pair of pieces goes into the gap of the other pair, so enters signals insertion

parts.note: to doctor something is to rig or tamper with it
a.m. marks times in the morning

explanation.surface: A physician arrives early one day at an old academic institute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' is a verb here, rig, not a medic.
explanation.definitionFit: Origami is the Japanese craft of folding paper into shapes, so the definition describes the activity.

clue.text: This might help when reading bank balance (nothing in it, repeatedly)

indicators.note: the letters for nothing are placed inside the abbreviation for bank, so in it signals insertion

parts.note: BK is a standard abbreviation for bank

indicators.note: the zero is used twice over, so repeatedly doubles it

parts.note: O, the figure zero, stands for nothing
rest is an old word for the balance or remainder

explanation.surface: A statement shows a bank balance with zeroes inside, as if someone is broke.
explanation.definitionFit: A bookrest is a stand that props a volume open, so it is a help to someone reading.

clue.text: 18 munching food

indicators.note: munching chews things up, so the letters are mashed into a new order

parts.note: the solution to 18 across is the compass direction east

explanation.surface: The Orient is pictured chewing its dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: Eats is informal slang for food, as in a place to get some eats.

clue.text: Functioning senior officer during alert damaged part of shirt

indicators.note: the officer phrase comes in the middle of the other letters, so during signals insertion
something damaged is knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a machine that is functioning is on
COL is the abbreviation for colonel, a senior army officer

explanation.surface: A high-ranking officer on duty during an alarm finds his shirt ripped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges ALERT to ETLAR, which goes round ONCOL.
explanation.definitionFit: An Eton collar is a broad stiff white collar worn outside the jacket, a detachable part of a boy's shirt.

clue.text: Abstract school character, ordinary initially

indicators.note: initially means take only the opening letter of the word ordinary

parts.note: a part is a character played by an actor

explanation.surface: A remark that some abstract school was ordinary at first in character.
explanation.definitionFit: Op art is a 1960s movement of abstract painting using optical illusions, so a school of abstract art.

clue.text: Ken's one thousand pounds present goes on house and wife

indicators.note: one piece is placed straight on after the other, so goes on joins them in order

parts.note: K, for kilo, is slang for a thousand pounds
the present time is now

explanation.surface: A man called Ken spends a thousand pounds on a gift that goes towards the house and his spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: Ken is not a name but the noun meaning range of knowledge; the 's is 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ken means knowledge or understanding, and know-how is practical expertise, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Family tension that a doctor might observe

parts.note: blood means family or kin, as in blood is thicker than water
pressure is stress or tension

explanation.surface: Strain within a family that a GP might notice in patients.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor routinely measures the force of circulation in the arteries with a cuff during a check-up.

clue.text: Ray and I then repaired toilet — a brief success

parts.note: a flash is a sudden ray of light

indicators.note: something repaired is put back together, here in a new order

parts.note: pan is slang for a toilet bowl

explanation.surface: Two people, Ray and the speaker, fix a lavatory and hope it lasts.
explanation.definitionFit: A flash in the pan is an idiom for a success that does not last, from a musket priming that fails to fire.

clue.text: Planned helper to intercept thug

indicators.note: the helper word cuts into the thug word, so to intercept signals insertion

parts.note: a lout is a rough uncouth thug
an aid is a helper or assistant

explanation.surface: An assistant has planned to stop a violent man in his tracks.
explanation.definitionFit: Laid out means arranged or designed beforehand, so planned, as with a garden or scheme.

clue.text: How food may be available to consumers experiencing continued fortune

definitions.text: How food may be available to consumers
definitions.meaning: a filling served in a bread bun, the way a sandwich-bar meal is sold
an idiom for enjoying a run of successes or good luck

explanation.surface: A café's menu promises lucky eaters something served in bread.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a filling in a bread bun; figuratively, a streak of luck or winning.

clue.text: In Algeria now, revolutionary's being broadcast

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns round, so the letters are read backwards
In says the letters sit inside the words Algeria now

explanation.surface: News of a radical figure in Algeria is on the airwaves right now.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme on the air is being transmitted live on radio or TV.

clue.text: Puts an end to European board game that's not finished

parts.note: a Scot is a European from Scotland

indicators.note: the game lacks its final letter, as if left incomplete

parts.note: chess is a game played on a board

explanation.surface: Someone from Europe abandons a board game before the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To scotch a plan or rumour is to stop it or kill it off, so to put an end to it.

clue.text: Unrefined report of horses current in north-east

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the words are said aloud

parts.note: fillies are young female horses; the Tyne is a river, a flowing current, in north-east England

explanation.surface: A news item about horses and electricity in the north-east of England.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tyne is the river flowing through Newcastle in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: A philistine is someone indifferent to art and culture, so as an adjective it means uncultured, unrefined.

clue.text: Commoner brought about heist, building old hideaway

indicators.note: the commoner word is brought round the other letters, so it signals a container

parts.note: a prole, short for proletarian, is a common working person

indicators.note: building constructs something, so the letters are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: An ordinary person stages a robbery while constructing a secret old hideaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'building' looks like the hideaway itself but is the anagram signal; prole is a dated, Orwellian word for a working-class person.
explanation.definitionFit: A priest hole was a secret chamber where Catholic priests hid during the persecutions of Tudor England.

clue.text: Amount of power by main road Asian runner's showing

parts.note: kW, the kilowatt, is a measure of power
the A1 is a major British road, written here with I for 1

explanation.surface: A power reading taken beside a highway in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is Britain's longest numbered road; in crosswords its 1 often becomes I.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kwai is a river in Thailand, and a runner is a crossword name for a river.

clue.text: Long to see cardinal running religious building

parts.note: to long for something is to pant for it
HE, His Eminence, is the title of a cardinal
a machine that is running is on

explanation.surface: Someone yearns to meet a Catholic prelate rushing about a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to see' is a link; the see also suits the bishop-like cardinal.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantheon is a temple dedicated to all the gods, so a building for worship.

clue.text: Son goes inside to devour course

indicators.note: the letter for son is placed within the other word

parts.note: to devour is to eat

explanation.surface: A boy comes indoors to wolf down his meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A course is a direction of travel, and east is one compass direction a ship might steer.

clue.text: Revd. jittery at station without fare?

parts.note: S is an abbreviation for station

indicators.note: something jittery shakes about, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A nervous vicar waits at a station without a ticket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jittery' rearranges REVDAT to TARVED. Fare means food here, not a ticket price.
explanation.definitionFit: To be starved is to go without food, and fare means the food served.

clue.text: Place to buy a group of boats, including American vessel

indicators.note: the boats word takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a fleet is a group of ships or boats
an ark is a vessel, like Noah's

explanation.surface: A shopper is told where to buy a flotilla with a US ship among them.
explanation.definitionFit: A flea market is an open-air market selling second-hand goods, so somewhere to shop.

clue.text: Artist returning inside liked interpreting Irish territory

indicators.note: the artist letters sit within the other letters
interpreting renders words differently, so the letters are rearranged
returning means the artist abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is a stock abbreviation for an artist

explanation.surface: A painter comes back and enjoys translating in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interpreting' looks like translation but is the anagram signal for liked; 'returning' turns the artist's letters, which then sit inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Kildare is a county in the Irish province of Leinster, so a region of Ireland.

clue.text: Celestial matter beginning to appear around South of France, westwards

indicators.note: the beginning word goes round the other letters

parts.note: to start is to begin to appear

indicators.note: in an across clue, westwards means read right to left

parts.note: sud is the French word for south

explanation.surface: Cosmic dust first shows up around the Midi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South of France' means the French word for south, not the region.
explanation.definitionFit: Stardust is fine particles drifting through space, so matter found among the heavens.

clue.text: Soldiers in school raised flag

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means read upwards, so backwards
the soldiers' letters go inside the school word

parts.note: a pod is a school of whales or dolphins
OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops at a school hoist a banner.
explanation.walkthrough: POORD read upwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To flag is to tire or wilt, as does to droop, so they are synonymous verbs.

clue.text: Clay slab covers edge of road sign in Spanish

indicators.note: the slab word covers the other letter, holding it inside

parts.note: a tile is a slab of baked clay

indicators.note: edge of picks the final letter of the word road

explanation.surface: A clay paver covers the side of a road where a Spanish sign stands.
explanation.definitionFit: The tilde is the wavy accent over n in Spanish words such as señor.

clue.text: An element travel up in excited eagerness

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol of silver, an element

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read backwards

parts.note: to go is to travel

explanation.surface: Someone is thrilled at a chemical element going up.
explanation.definitionFit: Agog means eagerly expectant and excited.

clue.text: Five biros laid regularly on artist's Italian table

indicators.note: in an across clue on means placed after, so the artist comes first

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is a stock abbreviation for an artist
V is the Roman numeral five

indicators.note: regularly means take every other letter of biros laid

explanation.surface: Five pens are set neatly on a painter's table in Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: Table here means food served, as in keeping a good table.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravioli are pasta parcels, a classic Italian dish, and table means fare served.

clue.text: Island emigre's half-eaten duck

indicators.note: with half eaten away, only the back half of emigre remains

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, and nada is Spanish for nothing

explanation.surface: An exile's duck dinner has been half consumed.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of emigre's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Grenada is a Caribbean island nation in the Windward group.

clue.text: Double act by two priests good in general, touring

parts.note: to do is to act

indicators.note: two means the priest letter appears twice

parts.note: P is an abbreviation for priest

indicators.note: the letter for good goes inside the other letters
touring takes things round about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Two clergymen do a turn touring with a general.
explanation.walkthrough: 'touring' rearranges GENERAL to ELANGER, with G placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A doppelganger is a person's double or lookalike.
